```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dari_2023b_ad26cov2s"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13025> (open access, PMC10583247)

Dari et al. pooled five Ad26.COV2.S trials (COV1001, COV1002, COV2001,
COV3001, COV3009) in SARS-CoV-2-seronegative adults who received
5 x 10^10 viral particles (vp) either once or as a prime plus a homologous
booster 2, 3 or 6 months later. They fit one mechanistic model of the humoral
immune response jointly to the spike-binding antibody (S-ELISA, EU/mL) and the
wild-type-virus neutralizing antibody (wtVNA, IC50 titer), and projected
antibody persistence to 24 months.

The model extends the single-dose model of the same group
(`Dari_2023_ad26cov2s_selisa`, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2023) by splitting the B-cell
response into two pathways (Eq. 1-7, Figure 1):

* a K-PD virtual antigen compartment (`antigen`), decaying at `k_ag`;
* a memory-B-cell pathway (`bcell_memory`, M1): antigen-driven and
  antigen-independent (`kp_m`) logistic growth to `n_mem`, differentiating into
  short-lived plasma cells (`plasma_short`) at `kp_s * antigen`;
* a germinal-centre pathway (`germinal_center`, M2): antigen-driven logistic
  growth to `n_gc`, differentiating into long-lived plasma cells
  (`plasma_long`) at `kp_l * antigen`;
* antibody secretion (`kab_s`, `kab_l`) into serum (`antibody`), distribution to
  a peripheral compartment (`antibody_periph`) and elimination (`ke_ab`).

The binding antibody is the output `Cc`. The neutralizing titer `wtvna` is
derived from it through a neutralizing-to-binding ratio with a decaying IgM
part (Eq. 8) and a log10 slope (Eq. 9). Age lowers both antibody production
rates and female sex raises the long-lived-plasma-cell production rate.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Dari_2023b_ad26cov2s")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
lloq <- c(selisa = 50.3, wtvna = 58) # Methods, 'Immunogenicity assays'
sd_s <- ui$theta[["expSd"]] # natural-log residual SD, S-ELISA
sd_v <- ui$theta[["expSd_wtvna"]] # natural-log residual SD, wtVNA
regimens <- c(
  "Single dose" = NA,
  "Booster (D1, D57)" = 56,
  "Booster (D1, D85)" = 84,
  "Booster (D1, D183)" = 182
)
```

# Population

The analysis pooled 5,608 S-ELISA samples from 978 participants and 1,882 wtVNA
samples from a subset of 375 participants, with data up to 15 months after the
prime. From Table S1: the S-ELISA set had a median age of 55 years (range
18-84; mean 52.2, SD 17.0), 48.6% women, 44.7% aged >= 60 years, median weight
73.8 kg, and was 72.8% White non-Hispanic, 12.3% Asian and 14.9% other race.
The wtVNA subset had a median age of 47 years (range 18-80), 45.9% women and
27.7% Asian participants. Boosters were given on days 25-70 (2 months), 70-130
(3 months) or after day 130 (6 months). Participants who became infected with
SARS-CoV-2 were withdrawn from that point. The same information is in the
model's `population` metadata.

# Source trace

Every value is a Table 1 entry of Dari 2023b unless stated otherwise; the
in-file comments in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Dari_2023b_ad26cov2s.R` carry
the same trace.

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `k_ag` (1/day) | 0.065 (fixed) | Table 1 'kAg' |
| `kp_ag` (cells/antigen unit/day) | 1 (fixed) | Table 1 'kpAg' |
| `kp_m` (1/day) | 0.0167 | Table 1 'kpM' |
| `ke_m`, `ke_gc` (1/day) | 0 (fixed) | Table 1 'keM1 and keM2' |
| `n_mem` (cells) | 10.7 x 10^4 (fixed) | Table 1 'N1' |
| `n_gc` (cells) | 0.129 x 10^4 | Table 1 'N2' |
| `kp_s`, `kp_l` (1/day/antigen unit) | 0.5 x 10^-5 each (fixed) | Table 1 'kpS', 'kpL' |
| `ke_s` (1/day) | 0.578 (fixed) | Table 1 'keS' |
| `ke_l` (1/day) | 19.1 x 10^-4 | Table 1 'keL'; unit printed /year, see below |
| `kab_s`, age 55 ((EU/mL)/cell/day) | 3.01 | Table 1 'kAbS' |
| `kab_l`, male aged 55 ((EU/mL)/cell/day) | 0.394 | Table 1 'kAbL' |
| `kab_p`, `kp_ab`, `ke_ab` (1/day) | 0.2075, 0.2716, 0.0556 (fixed) | Table 1 |
| `alpha_wtvna` | 0.732 | Table 1 'alpha'; Results 'Correlation between S-ELISA and wtVNA' |
| `beta_wtvna` (IC50 per EU/mL) | 3.85 | Table 1 'beta' |
| `igm_wtvna` (IC50 per EU/mL) | 6.10 | Table 1 'IgM' |
| `kigm` (1/day) | 0.0368 | Table 1 'kIgM' |
| `e_age_kab_s`, `e_age_kab_l` | -0.221, -0.867 | Table 1; power model `(AGE/55)^e`, Appendix S1 'Covariate analysis' |
| `e_sexf_kab_l` | 0.816 | Table 1; form `kAbL * (1 + e * SEXF)`, Appendix S1 |
| IIV `kab_s`, `kab_l` (CV) | 127%, 126% | Table 1; `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` (footnote a) |
| Residual SD (log10 scale) | 0.21 (S-ELISA), 0.238 (wtVNA) | Table 1 'Proportional error' (footnote c); Appendix S1 'Additive error model' |
| Antigen dose (`amt`) | 500 (x 10^8 vp) per dose | Not stated; see 'Antigen dose scale' |
| ODEs | Eq. 1-7 | Methods, 'Structural model' |
| wtVNA link | Eq. 8-9 | Methods, 'Structural model'; see 'Neutralizing-antibody link' |

# Shared helpers

```{r helpers}
# One dosing record per vaccination plus observation records. The model has
# two endpoints and neither is an ODE state, so observation rows carry
# dvid = 1 and no compartment; rxSolve still returns both Cc and wtvna.
make_events <- function(AGE, SEXF, boost, obs_times, amt = 500) {
  n <- length(AGE)
  covs <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), AGE = AGE, SEXF = SEXF)
  dose_times <- c(0, boost[!is.na(boost)])
  dose <- expand.grid(time = dose_times, id = seq_len(n))
  dose$evid <- 1L
  dose$amt <- amt
  dose$cmt <- "antigen"
  dose$dvid <- NA_integer_
  obs <- expand.grid(time = obs_times, id = seq_len(n))
  obs$evid <- 0L
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$cmt <- NA_character_
  obs$dvid <- 1L
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::left_join(covs, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

# Age drawn from the Table S1 S-ELISA distribution (mean 52.2, SD 17.0,
# truncated to the observed 18-84 years), as the paper sampled age from the
# analysis dataset.
sample_age <- function(n, lower = 18, upper = 84) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    a <- rnorm(2 * n, 52.2, 17.0)
    out <- c(out, a[a >= lower & a <= upper])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

typical <- function(m, boost, times, amt = 500) {
  ev <- make_events(AGE = 55, SEXF = 0.5, boost = boost, obs_times = times, amt = amt)
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(m), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
}
```

# Antigen dose scale

Table 1 gives `kp_ag` in cells/vp/day and `kp_s`, `kp_l` in 1/day/vp, but the
paper never states the number entered as the antigen dose. The same gap exists
in the single-dose paper, where 10^8 vp was the only power-of-ten unit that
reproduced the data. The maintainers repeated that check here: the
typical-value model (age 55, sex weight 0.5) was solved for each power-of-ten
unit of the nominal dose and compared with the simulated medians of the
Figure 3 VPC (black lines, digitised to about +/- 0.1 log10). Panel (d) is
left out: its 6-month booster arm has about 15 participants whose boosters fall
anywhere after day 130, so its pre-booster bin is not a single-dose curve.

```{r dose-scale}
fig3_median <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,            ~time, ~fig3_log10,
  "Single dose",          14, 2.27,
  "Single dose",          28, 2.60,
  "Single dose",          56, 2.72,
  "Single dose",          91, 2.78,
  "Single dose",         175, 2.60,
  "Single dose",         259, 2.62,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",    14, 2.22,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",    28, 2.55,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",    91, 3.37,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",   175, 3.15,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",   259, 2.93,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",    14, 2.30,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",    28, 2.60,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",   112, 3.35,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",   175, 3.07,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",   259, 2.98
)

dose_units <- c(
  "1e9 vp (amt = 50)" = 50,
  "1e8 vp (amt = 500)" = 500,
  "1e7 vp (amt = 5000)" = 5000,
  "vp (amt = 5e10)" = 5e10
)
scale_check <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(dose_units), function(u) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(unique(fig3_median$regimen), function(r) {
    typical(mod, regimens[[r]], sort(unique(fig3_median$time)), amt = dose_units[[u]]) |>
      dplyr::select(time, Cc) |>
      dplyr::mutate(regimen = r)
  })) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose_unit = u)
})) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig3_median, by = c("regimen", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = log10(Cc) - fig3_log10)

scale_fit <- scale_check |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_unit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_abs_log10_diff = mean(abs(diff)), .groups = "drop")
scale_fit |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose unit" = dose_unit, "Mean |difference| (log10)" = mean_abs_log10_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value S-ELISA vs the Figure 3 VPC median, by candidate dose unit.")

# Deterministic typical-value solves. Only the 10^8-vp unit lands within a
# few tenths of a log10 of the Figure 3 median; its neighbours miss by more
# than one log10.
fit_of <- function(u) scale_fit$mean_abs_log10_diff[scale_fit$dose_unit == u]
stopifnot(
  fit_of("1e8 vp (amt = 500)") < 0.2,
  fit_of("1e9 vp (amt = 50)") > 1,
  fit_of("1e7 vp (amt = 5000)") > 1,
  fit_of("vp (amt = 5e10)") > 1
)
```

Each 5 x 10^10 vp dose is therefore entered as `amt = 500`.

# Virtual cohorts

The main cohort has 200 participants per regimen, with age drawn as above and
a 1:1 sex ratio (the paper's simulation design). Observations are weekly to
day 728 (26 four-week months), so the same solve serves the VPC, the
exploratory geometric means and the persistence rule. Residual error is added
on the log scale with the model's own residual SDs, giving `Cc_obs` and
`wtvna_obs`.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2023)
set.seed(2023)
n_arm <- 200
obs_days <- seq(0, 728, by = 7)

sim_regimen <- function(m, boost, AGE, SEXF) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(m, make_events(AGE, SEXF, boost, obs_days), returnType = "data.frame")
}
sim_main <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(r) {
  sim_regimen(mod, regimens[[r]], sample_age(n_arm), rep(0:1, length.out = n_arm)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = r)
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Cc_obs = Cc * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_s)),
    wtvna_obs = wtvna * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_v))
  )
stopifnot(all(c("AGE", "SEXF") %in% names(sim_main)))
```

# Figure 3 and Figure S3: visual predictive checks

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 7}
vpc <- sim_main |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc_obs, wtvna_obs), names_to = "assay", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(assay = ifelse(assay == "Cc_obs", "S-ELISA (EU/mL)", "wtVNA (IC50)")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, assay, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(log10(value), 0.05),
    q50 = quantile(log10(value), 0.50),
    q95 = quantile(log10(value), 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens)))

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = fig3_median |> dplyr::mutate(assay = "S-ELISA (EU/mL)", regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens))),
    aes(time, fig3_log10), colour = "red"
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    data = data.frame(assay = c("S-ELISA (EU/mL)", "wtVNA (IC50)"), y = log10(lloq)),
    aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed", colour = "navy"
  ) +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ assay) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 450)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first vaccination (days)", y = "log10 titer",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 3 (S-ELISA) and Figure S3 (wtVNA) of Dari 2023b.",
      "Red points: digitised Figure 3 simulated medians; dashed line: LLOQ."
    )
  )

vpc_check <- vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(assay == "S-ELISA (EU/mL)") |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig3_median, by = c("regimen", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = q50 - fig3_log10)
stopifnot(nrow(vpc_check) == nrow(fig3_median))
vpc_check |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, time, q50, fig3_log10, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Day" = time, "Simulated median" = q50,
    "Figure 3 median" = fig3_log10, "Difference" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated vs digitised Figure 3 median (log10 EU/mL).")

# The simulated median has a sampling SD of about 0.05 log10 at n = 200. A
# mis-transcribed production rate, dose or covariate shifts it by > 0.3.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(vpc_check$diff)) < 0.2,
  quantile(abs(vpc_check$diff), 0.9) < 0.3
)
```

The simulated medians run about 0.1 log10 below the Figure 3 medians after the
peak. The paper's VPC replays the observed design (actual booster days and the
covariates of the participants sampled at each visit), which this simulation
does not.

# Neutralizing-antibody link (Eq. 8-9)

Eq. 8 defines the neutralizing-to-binding ratio
`beta + IgM * exp(-kIgM * time)` and Eq. 9 a log10 slope `alpha` without
intercept, but the paper does not write the combined expression. Two
compositions are possible:

* (A) the slope applies to the ratio-adjusted level:
  `log10(wtVNA) = alpha * log10(ratio * Ab)`;
* (B) the ratio multiplies the slope-transformed level:
  `log10(wtVNA) = log10(ratio) + alpha * log10(Ab)`.

The model uses (A). Figure 2b plots `log10(wtVNA / S-ELISA)` over time since
the first vaccination, and the Supplementary Results give the observed wtVNA
geometric-mean peaks, so both readings can be checked against the paper
without fitting. Time in Eq. 8 is time since the first vaccination, as in
Figure 2b.

```{r wtvna-link}
# Figure 2b medians (red solid line), digitised to about +/- 0.05.
fig2b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~fig2b_log_ratio,
  14, 0.00,
  28, -0.15,
  56, -0.28,
  91, -0.35,
  175, -0.35,
  259, -0.33,
  385, -0.30
)
alpha <- exp(ui$theta[["lalpha_wtvna"]])
beta <- exp(ui$theta[["lbeta_wtvna"]])
igm <- exp(ui$theta[["ligm_wtvna"]])
kigm <- exp(ui$theta[["lkigm"]])

link_cmp <- sim_main |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% fig2b$time) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ratio = beta + igm * exp(-kigm * time),
    log_ratio_A = log10(wtvna) - log10(Cc),
    log_ratio_B = log10(ratio) + (alpha - 1) * log10(Cc)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    reading_A = median(log_ratio_A),
    reading_B = median(log_ratio_B),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2b, by = "time")
knitr::kable(
  link_cmp |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Day" = time, "(A) model" = reading_A, "(B) alternative" = reading_B,
      "Figure 2b" = fig2b_log_ratio
    ),
  digits = 2, caption = "Median log10(wtVNA / S-ELISA) by day since the first vaccination."
)
# Reading (A) tracks Figure 2b to within a few hundredths of a log10;
# reading (B) sits 0.15-0.25 log10 too high at every visit. Both are medians
# of individual predictions over the same 800 participants, so the gap is
# stable across random draws.
stopifnot(
  mean(abs(link_cmp$reading_A - link_cmp$fig2b_log_ratio)) < 0.06,
  mean(abs(link_cmp$reading_B - link_cmp$fig2b_log_ratio)) > 0.12
)
```

# Exploratory geometric means

The Results ('S-ELISA and wtVNA geometric mean levels') and the Supplementary
Results report the observed geometric mean (GM) at the post-vaccination peak
and 140-160 days after the second peak (days after the single peak for the
single dose), with values below the LLOQ imputed to the LLOQ. The same summary
is computed on the simulated observations.

```{r geometric-means}
gm_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,             ~assay,    ~paper_peak, ~paper_cth,
  "Single dose",        "S-ELISA",  543,  343,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",  "S-ELISA", 1760,  606,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",  "S-ELISA", 2056,  810,
  "Booster (D1, D183)", "S-ELISA", 2674, 1407,
  "Single dose",        "wtVNA",    271,  221,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",  "wtVNA",    584,  238,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",  "wtVNA",    854,  245,
  "Booster (D1, D183)", "wtVNA",    944,  582
)

gm_sim <- sim_main |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 450) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc_obs, wtvna_obs), names_to = "assay", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    assay = ifelse(assay == "Cc_obs", "S-ELISA", "wtVNA"),
    value = pmax(value, ifelse(assay == "S-ELISA", lloq[["selisa"]], lloq[["wtvna"]]))
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, assay, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(gm = exp(mean(log(value))), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    data.frame(regimen = names(regimens), last_dose = ifelse(is.na(regimens), 0, regimens)),
    by = "regimen"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(time > last_dose) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, assay) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_peak = max(gm),
    t_peak = time[which.max(gm)],
    sim_cth = gm[which.min(abs(time - (t_peak + 150)))],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

gm_cmp <- gm_obs |>
  dplyr::inner_join(gm_sim, by = c("regimen", "assay")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    peak_ratio = sim_peak / paper_peak,
    cth_ratio = sim_cth / paper_cth
  )
gm_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, assay, paper_peak, sim_peak, paper_cth, sim_cth) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Assay" = assay, "Observed peak GM" = paper_peak,
    "Simulated peak GM" = sim_peak, "Observed GM 140-160 d after peak" = paper_cth,
    "Simulated GM 150 d after peak" = sim_cth
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Observed (Dari 2023b) vs simulated geometric means.")

# Observed GMs come from small, design-dependent subsets, so the check is on
# the centre of the ratios: a dose-scale or production-rate error moves every
# ratio by a factor of 3 or more. The 6-month booster arm (about 15
# participants from one study) is shown but not gated; see the text below.
gm_gate <- gm_cmp |> dplyr::filter(regimen != "Booster (D1, D183)")
log_ratios <- log10(c(gm_gate$peak_ratio, gm_gate$cth_ratio))
stopifnot(
  abs(median(log_ratios)) < 0.15,
  quantile(abs(log_ratios), 0.9) < 0.25
)
```

For the single dose and the 2- and 3-month boosters, the simulated geometric
means agree with the observed ones to within about 40%. The 6-month booster arm
does not: the simulated peak is about twice the observed one, and the level
150 days later is about half. That arm has about 15 participants (Results,
'Projected persistence of humoral immune responses'). The paper's own VPC
(Figure 3d) replays those participants' covariates, and its simulated median is
about 3.0 log10 before the booster and 3.2 log10 at day 365, well above the
typical curve of a 55-year-old. Covariates shift the post-booster curve by an
amount of that order. The typical-value solve below shows this for a
30-year-old participant (sex weight 0.5), compared with the Figure 3d
simulated median.

```{r figure-3d}
fig3d <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~fig3d_log10,
  28, 2.72,
  175, 3.00,
  210, 3.52,
  365, 3.18
)
panel_d <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typical(mod, 182, fig3d$time) |> dplyr::mutate(age = "55 years (reference)"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
    make_events(AGE = 30, SEXF = 0.5, boost = 182, obs_times = fig3d$time),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(age = "30 years")
) |>
  dplyr::select(age, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(log10_Cc = log10(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig3d, by = "time")
panel_d |>
  dplyr::select(age, time, log10_Cc, fig3d_log10) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age" = age, "Day" = time, "Typical log10 S-ELISA" = log10_Cc,
    "Figure 3d simulated median" = fig3d_log10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "6-month booster: typical-value S-ELISA by age vs Figure 3d.")
```

# Table 2 and Table S2: persistence above the LLOQ

The paper defines individual persistence as the time from vaccination until the
last titer above the LLOQ before two consecutive monthly titers below it, and
reports the share of participants still persisting at 8, 12, 18 and 24 months.
The simulation applies that rule to the four-weekly simulated observations
(including residual error) of the main cohort.

```{r persistence-helpers}
month_days <- 28 * (1:26)
landmarks <- c(8, 12, 18, 24)

# Time of the first of two consecutive below-LLOQ titers; Inf if there is none.
first_below_pair <- function(time, below) {
  k <- which(below[-length(below)] & below[-1])
  if (length(k) == 0) Inf else time[k[1]]
}

persistence <- function(sim, ys, yv, by = "regimen") {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(time %in% month_days) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(by)), id, time) |>
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c(by, "id")))) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      end_s = first_below_pair(time, .data[[ys]] < lloq[["selisa"]]),
      end_v = first_below_pair(time, .data[[yv]] < lloq[["wtvna"]]),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(month = landmarks) |>
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(c(by, "month")))) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      selisa = 100 * mean(end_s > month * 30.4375),
      wtvna = 100 * mean(end_v > month * 30.4375),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r persistence}
# Predicted % above the LLOQ for the overall population, Dari 2023b Table 2
# (S-ELISA) and Table S2 (wtVNA). The 8-month row is day 239 in Table 2.
paper_pers <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,             ~month, ~selisa, ~wtvna,
  "Single dose",             8,   93.5,   87.5,
  "Single dose",            12,   87.9,   78.4,
  "Single dose",            18,   80.0,   66.8,
  "Single dose",            24,   70.5,   55.2,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",       8,   99.9,   99.3,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",      12,   97.6,   94.5,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",      18,   94.3,   87.9,
  "Booster (D1, D57)",      24,   89.9,   80.3,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",       8,  100.0,   99.4,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",      12,   98.2,   95.3,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",      18,   94.7,   88.4,
  "Booster (D1, D85)",      24,   90.4,   81.0,
  "Booster (D1, D183)",      8,   95.6,   89.0,
  "Booster (D1, D183)",     12,   95.6,   89.0,
  "Booster (D1, D183)",     18,   93.9,   85.3,
  "Booster (D1, D183)",     24,   90.8,   80.0
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(selisa, wtvna), names_to = "assay", values_to = "paper_pct")

pers_cmp <- persistence(sim_main, "Cc_obs", "wtvna_obs") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(selisa, wtvna), names_to = "assay", values_to = "sim_pct") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(paper_pers, by = c("regimen", "month", "assay")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = sim_pct - paper_pct)
stopifnot(nrow(pers_cmp) == nrow(paper_pers))

pers_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(assay, regimen, month) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Assay" = assay, "Regimen" = regimen, "Month" = month,
    "Simulated %" = sim_pct, "Paper %" = paper_pct, "Difference" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Predicted percentage of participants with persisting titers above the LLOQ.")

ggplot(
  pers_cmp |> dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens))),
  aes(month, sim_pct, colour = regimen)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = paper_pct), shape = 4, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~assay, labeller = as_labeller(c(selisa = "S-ELISA", wtvna = "wtVNA"))) +
  labs(
    x = "Months after the first vaccination", y = "% of participants above LLOQ",
    caption = "Lines: simulation; crosses: Dari 2023b Table 2 and Table S2."
  )

# 200 participants per regimen give a sampling SD of 2-3 percentage points
# per cell, and the cells of one regimen move together because they share
# subjects. A 2,000-per-regimen run sits about 3 points above the paper (see
# the text below). A dose unit one power of ten off, or the alternative
# readings checked further down, move whole regimens by 10-25 points.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(pers_cmp$diff)) < 6,
  quantile(abs(pers_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

The simulated persistence follows Table 2 and Table S2 across regimens and
reproduces the headline ordering: a steady decline after a single dose, and a
24-month persistence near 90% (S-ELISA) and 80-85% (wtVNA) after any
booster. The simulation runs a few points high, by about 3 points in a
2,000-per-regimen run and most for the single dose and the 6-month booster
arm. The paper also sampled parameter uncertainty, which widens the titer
distribution and moves more participants below the LLOQ; this vignette
simulates the point estimates only. The largest single gap is the 6-month
booster at 8 months (paper 95.6% / 89.0%), which in the paper equals its
12-month value: those participants lost persistence before the booster, when
only the prime had been given.

# Figure 4: men aged 60 years and older

The paper's most-quoted subgroup is men aged >= 60 years: 24-month persistence
after a single dose of 50.7% (S-ELISA) and 34.3% (wtVNA), rising to at least
79.7% and 64.7% after any booster (Results, Figure 4).

```{r men-60}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(60)
set.seed(60)
sim_m60 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(regimens), function(r) {
  sim_regimen(mod, regimens[[r]], sample_age(n_arm, lower = 60), rep(0, n_arm)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = r)
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    eps_s = rnorm(dplyr::n()),
    eps_v = rnorm(dplyr::n()),
    Cc_obs = Cc * exp(sd_s * eps_s),
    wtvna_obs = wtvna * exp(sd_v * eps_v)
  )
m60 <- persistence(sim_m60, "Cc_obs", "wtvna_obs") |>
  dplyr::filter(month == 24)
m60 |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(regimen) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Month" = month, "S-ELISA %" = selisa, "wtVNA %" = wtvna) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated 24-month persistence, men aged >= 60 years.")

single60 <- m60[m60$regimen == "Single dose", ]
boost60 <- m60[m60$regimen != "Single dose", ]
# Across random draws each cell varies with an SD of about 5 points at
# n = 200, and the point-estimate simulation runs about 5 points above the
# paper here (see the persistence section). The check is on the mean of the
# four differences; the per-cell bound only catches a gross error. The
# alternative readings below move the single-dose cells by 10-35 points.
m60_diff <- c(
  single60$selisa - 50.7,
  single60$wtvna - 34.3,
  min(boost60$selisa) - 79.7,
  min(boost60$wtvna) - 64.7
)
stopifnot(
  abs(mean(m60_diff)) < 12,
  max(abs(m60_diff)) < 25
)
```

# Readings not printed in the paper

Two Table 1 entries need a reading the paper does not spell out. Both were
settled by the paper's own persistence projections, which depend on them
strongly; no value was fitted.

**Long-lived plasma-cell elimination `ke_l`.** Table 1 prints
19.1 x 10^-4 with the unit "year^-1", the unit of the row above it. The
single-dose paper estimated 16.8 x 10^-4 day^-1 for the same parameter. Read
per year, the long-lived plasma cells barely decline over 24 months (half-life
363 years), titers plateau and the single-dose persistence cannot fall from
93.5% to 70.5% as Table 2 reports.

**Residual error scale.** Appendix S1 states an additive error on log10 titers,
while Table 1 labels the values "Proportional error" 21 (S-ELISA) and 23.8
(wtVNA) in a CV% column (footnote c: "refers to original values, i.e. additive
error on log-transformed values"). The model reads them as log10-scale SDs x 100
(0.21 and 0.238), the reading that also fit the single-dose paper. Read as CVs
on the original scale (natural-log SD 0.207 and 0.235) the residual noise around
the LLOQ shrinks, and the persistence of men aged >= 60 years no longer falls
as far as Figure 4 shows.

```{r readings}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(7)
set.seed(7)
mod_kel_year <- mod |> rxode2::ini(lke_l = log(19.1e-4 / 365.25))
sim_year <- sim_regimen(mod_kel_year, NA, sample_age(n_arm), rep(0:1, length.out = n_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    regimen = "Single dose",
    Cc_obs = Cc * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_s)),
    wtvna_obs = wtvna * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, sd_v))
  )
pers_year <- persistence(sim_year, "Cc_obs", "wtvna_obs")

# CV reading of the residual: same individual predictions and the same
# standard-normal draws as the men >= 60 cohort, smaller SDs.
sd_s_cv <- sqrt(log(1 + 0.21^2))
sd_v_cv <- sqrt(log(1 + 0.238^2))
m60_cv <- sim_m60 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Cc_cv = Cc * exp(sd_s_cv * eps_s),
    wtvna_cv = wtvna * exp(sd_v_cv * eps_v)
  ) |>
  persistence("Cc_cv", "wtvna_cv") |>
  dplyr::filter(month == 24, regimen == "Single dose")

readings <- tibble::tribble(
  ~check, ~assay, ~paper,
  "Single dose, 24 months, all", "S-ELISA", 70.5,
  "Single dose, 24 months, all", "wtVNA", 55.2,
  "Single dose, 24 months, men >= 60", "S-ELISA", 50.7,
  "Single dose, 24 months, men >= 60", "wtVNA", 34.3
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = c(
      pers_cmp$sim_pct[pers_cmp$regimen == "Single dose" & pers_cmp$month == 24 & pers_cmp$assay == "selisa"],
      pers_cmp$sim_pct[pers_cmp$regimen == "Single dose" & pers_cmp$month == 24 & pers_cmp$assay == "wtvna"],
      single60$selisa, single60$wtvna
    ),
    kel_per_year = c(
      pers_year$selisa[pers_year$month == 24], pers_year$wtvna[pers_year$month == 24],
      NA, NA
    ),
    residual_cv = c(NA, NA, m60_cv$selisa, m60_cv$wtvna)
  )
readings |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Check" = check, "Assay" = assay, "Paper %" = paper, "Model %" = model,
    "keL read per year %" = kel_per_year, "Residual read as CV %" = residual_cv
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Persistence under the model's readings and the alternatives.")

# keL per year leaves 24-month single-dose persistence above 90%, against
# 70.5% / 55.2% in the paper; the model sits within a few points. The CV
# reading overshoots the men >= 60 subgroup by about 8-12 points more than
# the log10 reading (same individuals, same draws).
stopifnot(
  readings$kel_per_year[1] - readings$paper[1] > 15,
  readings$kel_per_year[2] - readings$paper[2] > 15,
  mean(readings$residual_cv[3:4] - readings$model[3:4]) > 3
)
```

# PKNCA: peak antibody response

The paper reports no non-compartmental analysis. This block computes the
individual peak S-ELISA concentration after the last vaccination from the
simulated individual predictions (no residual error) and compares its median
with the observed geometric-mean peak of each regimen.

```{r pknca}
last_dose <- ifelse(is.na(regimens), 0, regimens)
nca_conc <- sim_main |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = paste(regimen, id)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
stopifnot(all(nca_conc$time[!duplicated(nca_conc$id)] == 0))

nca_dose <- nca_conc |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen) |>
  dplyr::left_join(data.frame(regimen = names(regimens), boost = regimens), by = "regimen") |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(dose_no = 1:2) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = ifelse(dose_no == 1, 0, boost), amt = 500) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(time)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, amt)

nca_int <- data.frame(
  regimen = names(regimens),
  start = unname(last_dose),
  end = unname(last_dose) + 150,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id),
  intervals = nca_int
))

nca_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax")) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
nca_ref <- data.frame(
  regimen = gm_obs$regimen[gm_obs$assay == "S-ELISA"],
  cmax = gm_obs$paper_peak[gm_obs$assay == "S-ELISA"]
)
nca_tbl <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_sim |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax"),
  nca_ref,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "EU/mL")
)
knitr::kable(nca_tbl, caption = "Median simulated S-ELISA Cmax after the last vaccination vs the observed geometric-mean peak.")

nca_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(regimen) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Median Cmax (EU/mL)" = cmax, "Median Tmax (day after last dose)" = tmax) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Simulated peak S-ELISA response.")
```

```{r pknca-footnote, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
fn <- attr(nca_tbl, "footnote")
if (!is.null(fn)) cat(fn)
```

The single-dose and 2-month booster peaks agree with the observed geometric
means to within about 15%, and the 3-month booster peak is about 30% higher.
The 6-month booster peak is well above the observed 2,674 EU/mL, for the
reasons given under 'Exploratory geometric means': in the model, memory B cells
keep expanding between the prime and the booster (`kp_m`, with no memory-B-cell
loss), so a later booster meets a larger memory pool. The paper reports a
4.92-fold rise in peak S-ELISA concentration after a 6-month booster, but that
observed rise comes from a small arm with its own covariate mix.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Antigen dose scale (not stated in the paper).** Each vaccine dose enters
  the K-PD antigen compartment as `amt = 500`, i.e. 5 x 10^10 vp in units of
  10^8 vp. The paper gives `kp_ag`, `kp_s` and `kp_l` per vp but never the
  amount entered. The maintainers compared each power-of-ten unit of the nominal
  dose and kept the only one that reproduces Figure 3 (see above). No
  continuous fitting was done.
- **`ke_l` unit.** Table 1 prints the long-lived plasma-cell elimination rate
  19.1 x 10^-4 with unit year^-1; the model reads it per day, as in the
  single-dose paper, because the per-year reading cannot produce the
  persistence decline of Table 2 and Table S2.
- **Residual error scale.** The Table 1 "Proportional error" entries are read as
  log10-scale SDs x 100 and encoded as `lnorm()` SDs on the natural-log scale
  (0.4835 and 0.5480), consistent with Appendix S1 and with the single-dose
  paper.
- **wtVNA link.** Eq. 8 and Eq. 9 are composed as
  `log10(wtVNA) = alpha * log10((beta + IgM * exp(-kIgM * t)) * Ab)`, the
  composition that reproduces Figure 2b. Time in the IgM term is time since the
  first vaccination, so a simulation must start at the prime.
- **Age effect.** Appendix S1 gives the continuous covariate model as a power
  of the covariate over its median (55 years). The Results quote decreases of
  23% (kAbS) and 64% (kAbL) between 23 and 84 years; the power model gives 25%
  and 68% over that range (the quoted figures match a lower percentile of about
  26 years). The printed equation is kept.
- **Persistence simulation.** The paper simulated 250,000 participants with
  parameter uncertainty; this vignette uses 200 participants per regimen and
  the point estimates. Age is drawn from a normal distribution with the
  Table S1 mean and SD truncated to 18-84 years.
- **Observation names.** The binding-antibody output is named `Cc`, as in the
  single-dose model and in `Dasti_2025_mrna1273_qsp`, although it is an
  antibody response and not a concentration of the administered vaccine. The
  neutralizing titer is `wtvna`.
- **Screened covariates.** Body weight, race and country were screened and not
  retained; body weight is listed in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- No erratum or correction notice for Dari 2023b was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-10-27.
